stories.headline: Senegal are reinstated as Africa Cup of Nations champions
stories.summary: Senegal beat the hosts, Morocco, 1–0 after extra time in the final of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations. In March the CAF Appeal Board ruled that they had forfeited the match by walking off the pitch, and awarded Morocco a 3–0 victory. On 24 November the Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled in Senegal's favour and reinstated them as the winners.

stories.headline: A Spanish economist is elected to lead the European Central Bank
stories.summary: Pablo Hernández de Cos has been elected as the new president of the European Central Bank. He succeeds Christine Lagarde, who resigned. He was the 70th governor of the Bank of Spain from 2018 to 2024, and has been general manager of the Bank for International Settlements since 1 July 2025.

stories.headline: SpaceX is cleared to launch up to a million satellites
stories.summary: The United States Federal Communications Commission has authorised SpaceX to deploy up to one million satellites for Starmind, its space-based data centre network. The satellites are solar-powered, would operate in a sun-synchronous orbit, and are to be launched on the company's Starship rocket. The decision was taken despite concerns about space debris and interference with astronomical objects.

stories.headline: A Scottish fossil turns out not to be an early reptile
stories.summary: A small fossil found in Scotland in 1984 was regarded for nearly three decades as one of the earliest known reptiles. A closer look inside the rock found a primitive skull, internal gills containing bone and a mouth resembling that of a fish, with thousands of tiny teeth. The animal, Westlothiana lizziae, is 345 million years old.
